safety_evidence.finding: with_current selects the timer slab from agent::current_agent(); purge_agent removes a whole agent slab. release_entries_in_freed_ranges currently scans all slabs, drops matching entries after unlocking, and republishes counters only for PRIMARY_AGENT.

CURRENT_AGENT is thread-local, starts unset (therefore PRIMARY_AGENT), and is set to a fresh worker id only by enter_worker_agent. enter_agent_for_test is public/doc-hidden and documented for tests only; no production callsites were found. retire_agent shuts down the worker loop, purges its timer slab, then retires other per-agent state before the arena is dropped.

parallel_map, parallel_filter, and spawn claim their own agent before allocations and call retire_agent after dropping their GC scope. spawn catches the body result/panic and then reaches retirement. The two direct closure-call paths use the non-unwinding JS body ABI. Workspace dev/release/distribution profiles use panic=abort, so an unexpected runtime panic cannot leave a surviving process with an unretired worker slab.
Worker thread enters its own agent before initialization; its worker body is caught, then retire_agent runs before thread return/arena destruction.
Freed-range hooks run during arena TLS teardown. They must not use TLS or call JS. Timer entry removal keeps drops outside the timer-store lock.

A newly spawned helper thread has no inherited CURRENT_AGENT, so timer operations on it are primary-partition operations. Only explicit enter_worker_agent (or test-only enter_agent_for_test) assigns a worker partition. Production worker creation sites establish and retire their worker agent; helper threads acting on primary state remain in PRIMARY_AGENT.

testability_constraint: The release_entries_in_freed_ranges wrapper is a no-op under cfg(test), because tests use per-thread stores. A focused test must exercise a private shared selection/removal helper also called by the production wrapper; do not test only the no-op wrapper.
limits: This source proof does not establish that nonworker helpers never queue callbacks into primary-owned timers whose values live in their own arenas; the primary scan remains necessary for that issue body concern.
The narrow change would remove scanning of unrelated worker slabs, not fix silently dropped callbacks or establish a measured speedup.

enter_agent_for_test is public but doc-hidden and explicitly documented as test-only; a source search found no production callsites. The GO therefore relies on that documented ownership contract; if arbitrary external callers are in scope, require a separate API restriction before claiming all worker slabs are purged.
